title: Disseqt AI raises $8 Mn led by Gresham House Ventures, Rahul Dravid joins round
summary:
AI governance and assurance startup Disseqt AI has raised $8 million in pre-Series A funding round led by Gresham House Ventures, with participation from existing investor Sure Valley Ventures (SVV), Delta Partners and Enterprise Ireland.

The round also saw participation from angel investors, including senior executives from OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce and Meta, along with former Indian cricket captain Rahul Dravid, who invested in his individual capacity.

The fresh funds will be utilized to expand its enterprise customer base globally and  hiring across sales, operations and technology roles in India, Disseqt said in a press release.

Founded in late 2025 by Apoorva Kumar, Manish Atri and Cyril Treacy, Disseqt AI provides an AI governance and assurance platform that helps enterprises test, monitor and govern AI applications and agents.

Its platform enables businesses to assess AI agents for vulnerabilities before deployment, enforce company policies once they go live, and continuously monitor their behaviour. It can also block outputs that violate organisational policies while maintaining audit trails for compliance and oversight.

The platform allows enterprises to test whether AI agents can be manipulated into revealing confidential customer information or exhibiting other vulnerabilities before being deployed in business operations.

The funding comes amid growing enterprise adoption of AI agents and increasing concerns around their safety, security and regulatory compliance. According to McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey, 40% of respondents at companies with annual revenues exceeding $1 billion were scaling AI agents in at least one business function, compared with 27% a year earlier.

Disseqt said it has already deployed its assurance capabilities across multiple enterprise use cases. In a project involving a global sports league's fan engagement agent, which serves 80 million fans, the company improved the safe-response rate from 80% to 99% across tests covering safety, bias and privacy risks. It added that no unsafe outputs were detected when the original failing tests were repeated after fixes.

The company also provides assurance services for a credit card services programme at a large European bank.

The investment marks another bet on the emerging AI governance and assurance segment, as enterprises look to deploy autonomous AI systems across customer interactions, financial services and internal business operations.
